messages:
alex w: Quick ask — can we get an OK to procure supplemental H100 capacity for next quarter?

alex w: Short context: inference traffic spiked after the last release (more long-context jobs). Current H100 pool (us-west2) is at ~92% util and our autoscaler is cold-starting more often. If we don't add capacity we'll see increased queuing and higher p99 latencies.

alex w: Proposal: one-time supplemental order of 8 H100s in us-west2 (reserved 1yr) + 4 burst H100s in us-west2 on convertible committed use for peak. Estimated incremental net commit: $156k/year.

infra-bot: h100-pool-us-west2 utilization=92% (5-min avg), queued-jobs=42, avg-queue-time=37s, p99-latency-up=21% from baseline.

jonathan r: Adding the perf numbers I promised yesterday — tail latency correlates with KV cache misses when sequence length > 8k. More nodes buys cache capacity which will reduce token recompute for those long jobs.

maya z: Need the financials. Can you post amortized $/GPU-hour and expected run rate? Also which budget code would this charge to?

alex w: Rough calc: reserved amortized $/h ~ $6.5 (after 1yr commitment discount), burst (convertible short-term) ~$18/h. Expected average consumption after procurement ~ 520 GPU-hours/day across cluster; incremental cost delta ~ $2.4k/day. (Will formalize in a spreadsheet).

jonathan r: Quick billing check I ran earlier:
```
SELECT SUM(cost) FROM billing.gcp WHERE sku LIKE '%H100%' AND region='us-west2' AND date >= '2025-10-01';
```
Results show H100 spend jumped 48% month-over-month.

sophie l: Two questions — can we shift some heavy long-context evals to a eu-central batch window (lower priority) to avoid buying all in us-west2? Also what about A100 mix for cheaper throughput on some models?

alex w: We evaluated A100 vs H100 for these workloads — H100 gives ~x1.7 throughput on our optimized kernels for long-context and reduced mem copy overhead. For short convo workloads A100 is fine, but these new long-context batch jobs are H100-bound. We can shift ~18% of runs to eu-central overnight but peak business hours are still us-west2.

maya z: For approval I need: 1) PO amount, 2) GL code, 3) expected ROI (reduced queueing = SLA improvement), 4) fallback plan if usage falls. Please add to the procurement PR.

alex w: Will open PR today. PO tentative: $156,000/year. GL code: PROD-INFRA-GPU-23 (confirming with finops). ROI: estimated p99 latency reduction 25-40% for long-context requests, saved token recompute cost ~ $0.12/token on those jobs (back-of-envelope). Fallback: convertible commitments can be resold/reconfigured to other regions; we can pause burst nodes.

finops-bot: Reminder — procurement over $100k requires exec approval + monthly forecast doc attached.

jonathan r: Timeline: if we submit the PR by EOD Tue and get finops + Eng manager OK by Fri, vendor lead time suggests provision in ~3 weeks.

sophie l: Can we TTL-tag new nodes to a canary namespace and route 10% of traffic for 72h before moving to 100%? If perf looks good we flip.

alex w: Yes — plan is canary 10% -> 72h metrics -> ramp 25% -> 72h -> full. Will include rollout in PR.

maya z: I'll review the PR, but preliminary OK from me pending final numbers and GL confirmation. :thumbsup:

alex w: Thanks — I'll ping when PR is up and include the spreadsheets and dashboard links.

infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-6789: "Supplemental H100 procurement — Q1" assigned to alex w.

jonathan r: tagging dakota for procurement ops FYI.

alex w: tagging @dakota for procurement ops and timeline help.

dakota (external): ack — will queue vendor quotes and share payment terms once PR created.

maya z: if procurement can secure convertible terms, we should prefer that to reduce downside.

alex w: noted. thanks all.
